textbookText: Section ‘D’ Long answer type questions. 1. Study the given diagram and answer the following questions: i) What is the secret of the fact that when a ball in thrown vertically up from either of the poles of the Earth, as shown in the above picture, the bulls always fall towards the surface of the Earth? Ans:- This happens because of Earth’s gravitational force. Gravity acts towards the center of the Earth, pulling any object dropped or thrown vertically back to the surface, regardless of the location (pole or equator). ii) The Sun, the Earth and the Moon are shown in the picture. The Earth revolves around the Sun and the Moon revolve around Earth. What is the reason for this? Ans:- The Earth revolves around the Sun due to the Sun’s gravitational pull, while the Moon revolves around the Earth due to Earth’s gravitational pull. iii) All these three celestial bodies have their gravity, but how is it possible for them to stay in their place? Ans:- Celestial bodies stay in their positions because of a balance between gravitational force and inertia. Their forward motion prevents them from falling directly into another body, while gravity keeps them in orbit. iv) Why planets and satellites do not collide with each other while moving in their orbits? Ans:- Planets and satellites do not collide because each moves in a specific orbit with a certain speed. The combination of gravity and orbital velocity keeps them in stable paths without collision. 2. Describe any two concept about the future of universe. Ans:- Two concept about the future of universe are given below, Big Freeze: The universe will continue expanding indefinitely, causing galaxies, stars, and planets to move farther apart. Over time, stars will burn out, galaxies will drift away, and the universe will become dark, cold, and empty, reaching a state of maximum entropy. Big Crunch: If the gravitational pull of matter in the universe is strong enough, the expansion may eventually slow down and reverse. This would cause all matter to collapse into a hot, dense state, possibly ending the universe in a massive implosion. 3. Write any four importance of gravitational force. Ans:- The four importance of gravitational force are, 1. Gravitational force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun and the Moon around the Earth. 2. It helps in the formation of stars, planets, and galaxies by pulling matter together. 3. Gravity holds the Earth’s atmosphere, making life possible. 4. The gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun causes tides in the oceans. 4. Explain the big-bang theory with diagram. Ans:- The Big Bang Theory explains the origin and evolution of the universe. According to this theory, about 13.8 billion years ago, the universe began from a singular point of extremely high temperature and density. This point suddenly expanded rapidly, causing the universe to grow in all directions. As it expanded, the universe cooled down, allowing matter to form stars, galaxies, and other cosmic structures. The universe continues to expand even today, with galaxies moving away from each other, supporting the idea of an ever-growing cosmos. 5. Study the given diagram about the types of universe and answer the following questions. (a) Which curve shows that the density of matter of the universe is equal to the critical density? Ans:- Curve B shows that the density of matter of the universe is equal to the critical density. This represents a flat universe that will expand forever but at a rate that slows down asymptotically. (b) In which condition universe shrink and occur the Big Crunch? Ans:- The universe will shrink and lead to the Big Crunch under the condition shown by curve C, where the density of the universe is greater than the critical density. This represents a closed universe that eventually collapses due to strong gravitational pull. (c) Which curve shows that the average density of the universe is less than the critical density? Write with reason. Ans:- Curve A shows that the average density of the universe is less than the critical density. This represents an open universe, where the expansion continues forever because the gravitational pull is not strong enough to stop it.
